title: Force-majeure clauses
summary: A force-majeure clause allocates the consequences of specified events that disrupt performance. Its wording can determine whether a party receives more, less, or different protection than a background excuse doctrine would provide.
notes:
Identify the listed events, any general catchall, the required effect on performance, notice requirements, mitigation duties, and the stated consequence. A clause may permit delay, suspension, or termination rather than erase all obligations. Causation matters: occurrence of an event does not by itself show that the event prevented the performance in dispute.

The syllabus calls for a force-majeure clause alongside the excuse cases. The casebook’s discussion supplies the conceptual setting. The force majeure clause the syllabus lists for assignment 21 was distributed in class and is not among the supplied files.
